W9.verified_by: the input is outline.docx precisely because it has NO header, NO footer and no reference to one in `w:sectPr` — running this against report.docx would exercise 'replace' while reporting 'create', and the four package pieces that make a new part reachable would never run. D1 is the assertion that owns this: it resolves every r:id in document.xml, so a `headerReference` written without its relationship fires there. F1/F2 hold the rest of the document still, D4 keeps `w:sectPr` last in the body (the reference is inserted INTO it, which is where the element order of CT_SectPr starts to matter), and D7 renders the result. ⚠️ `contains` names BODY text: a header lives in its own part and python-docx's `doc.paragraphs` never walks it, so asserting the header's own words there would fail on a correct artifact. What L2 cannot see — that a first-page header without `<w:titlePg/>` and an even-page header without `<w:evenAndOddHeaders/>` in settings.xml are parts Word simply ignores, so the capability is FIVE things and not four — is scripts/test-docx-skill.py H1-H5

W10.verified_by: D2 is doing real work here: a TOC is a field, and `w:fldChar`/`w:instrText`/`w:bookmarkStart` plus a nine-level `w:abstractNum` are four content models with strict child order that the XSD checks against the published schema rather than against this repo's opinion. D1 covers the bookmark-anchored hyperlinks, D4 the element order in the styles this creates, D7 that LibreOffice still lays it out. ⚠️ `paragraphs` is 16 and not 10 because a cached TOC result IS paragraphs — one per entry plus the title; a field with no result would leave it at 11. ⚠️ `contains` names the TOC TITLE and the headings' own text, never a TOC entry: entries live inside `w:hyperlink` and python-docx walks direct `w:r` children only, so asserting one would fail on a correct artifact for the same reason a tracked insertion does (gotchas §21.2 ㉔/㉛). The product decision L2 cannot see — that the cached result carries the heading text and NO page number, because a page number nothing has laid out is a guess, and that both `w:dirty` and `w:updateFields` are set so the reader is asked to compute the real ones — is scripts/test-docx-skill.py G1-G6, along with the half of outline numbering everybody forgets (the `w:abstractNum` alone numbers nothing; the heading STYLE has to carry the `w:numPr` too)

W11.verified_by: outline.docx declares no `<Default Extension="png">` and holds no word/media, so the sample is the create path and not the replace path: the picture needs the media part, a content-type Default for its extension, a relationship and a `wp:inline` drawing, and D1 fires if the `r:embed` resolves to nothing while D2 checks the drawing against the DrawingML schema. D7 is the one that catches an undeclared content type — LibreOffice renders a document Word would offer to repair. What none of them can see is the sizing: EMU are English Metric Units, 914400 to the inch, so filling the extent with a pixel count yields a thumbnail and filling it with a centimetre count yields a picture forty times the page. scripts/test-docx-skill.py M1-M5 assert the measured size against the PNG's own pHYs density, that the aspect ratio survives `--width-cm`, that the drawing extent and the inner `a:ext` agree (they are two numbers for one size and Word believes the outer one while LibreOffice draws the inner), and that replacing an image reuses the relationship instead of orphaning the old part

W16.verified_by: this is the one capability whose gate is D6 itself, used as a before/after pair: fontless.docx FAILS D6 with exactly three findings and the artifact must pass it, which is the same pairing W15 uses (a repair verified only on its output cannot be told apart from a check with no teeth). The three findings are three different defects on purpose — a run with no `w:rPr` at all, a run whose paragraph STYLE already names a face, and a run carrying `@w:ascii` and no `@w:eastAsia` — and they do not have the same right answer. scripts/test-docx-skill.py N1-N5 assert that the inherited case takes the STYLE's face and not the fallback (writing 宋体 over a heading the document already said should be 黑体 is a silent restyle that D6 cannot distinguish from a repair), that a deliberate latin face survives, that `--check` on an already-correct document reports nothing and writes nothing, and that `--strict` refuses when a value came from the fallback because nothing in the file said what face that text wants

W12.verified_by: the artifact differs from its input in exactly one part — word/styles.xml — so F1/F2 are the assertion that the rest of the document was not touched, and D2 checks the new `w:style` against CT_Style's child order, which is a strict sequence this skill has to get right by construction rather than by remembering. D1/D4/D7 cover the package, the element order and the render. What L2 cannot see is the whole contract, because none of it is visible in a legal document: that MODIFYING a style repaints every paragraph using it (so `--set` on an existing id refuses without `--overwrite`, and the report says how many), that DELETING one Word silently replaces with Normal (so it refuses unless nothing uses it or `--reassign` says where they go), that a `w:basedOn` cycle makes Word stop resolving formatting with no error anywhere, and that a style based on a deleted one must be repointed rather than left dangling. scripts/test-docx-skill.py S1-S5 assert each, and S3 in particular pins a defect this skill shipped and fixed within the hour: the report said `properties_set: []` on a call that set six — the document was right and the REPORT was wrong, which is the harder half to notice

W4.verified_by: there is no `baseline` because nothing was edited — this capability builds a package from nothing, so F1/F2 have no input to compare against and say so rather than pretending. That puts the whole weight on the legality checks, which is the right place for it: D2 validates every part of a hand-built package against the ECMA-376 schemas (the reason this authors its own blank document instead of starting from python-docx's template, which ships a `w:zoom` without the required `w:percent` and would fail here — gotchas §21.2 ㉗), D1 that the hyperlink and image relationships resolve, D4 that `w:sectPr` is still last after fifteen blocks were appended, D6 that every generated CJK run binds both faces, and D7 that LibreOffice lays it out non-blank. What none of them can see is the contract: that a construct this cannot map is REPORTED with its line number rather than dropped — the sample's Markdown carries a footnote and two raw HTML tags on purpose, so a generator that silently discarded them would still produce a legal document and pass everything above. scripts/test-docx-skill.py D1-D6 assert that, plus that `--strict` refuses and writes nothing, that the styles a `w:pStyle` names are actually created (naming one that does not exist is valid XML that silently formats as Normal), that nested list levels reach the numbering they claim, and that `--template` keeps a house style's parts while replacing only the body
